text: Pampered means treated with extra care and given every comfort. Here, royals gave their little dogs the best of everything.
Indolent means lazy, someone who likes to lounge around and avoids work. Here, Lady Bertram is a character who does very little.
To dote on someone is to love them so much that you give them lots of attention and care. Here, people spoil their dogs more than before.
An epitaph is a short message written or carved to remember someone who has died, often on a gravestone. The Romans wrote them for pets too.
A stock character is a type of person that shows up again and again in stories, with the same few traits. Here, it is the mother who cares more about her dog than her children.
Napoleon Bonaparte was a famous French general who later became emperor of France. He lived from 1769 to 1821.
Plucky means brave and determined, even when a task looks hard or you are small. Here, it describes the young general.
A bedchamber is an old-fashioned word for a bedroom, especially in a palace or a big house.
A pug is a small dog with a flat, wrinkly face and a curly tail.
To dictate is to give orders that others must follow. Here, the quote jokes that a man who ruled Europe could not even order a dog out of his room.
A biographer is a writer who tells the story of a real person's life.
A historian is a person who studies the past and writes about it.
This is a joke. A pawprint is a dog's footprint, and outsize means bigger than expected. It means small dogs left a big mark on history.
A blueprint is a detailed plan that shows how to build something. Here, it means small dogs were the model for how we treat pets today.
To sprawl is to sit or lie with your arms and legs spread out in a lazy way.
A pomeranian is a very small, fluffy dog with a thick coat.
Greedy here means always wanting more food. It is a loving way to describe a dog that licks and begs for treats.
Pliny the Elder was a Roman writer who lived about 2,000 years ago and wrote about nature, including many ideas that turned out to be wrong.
To reckon is to think or believe something. Here, Pliny believed a dog could take away a stomachache.
Mary Queen of Scots was a queen of Scotland who was put to death in 1587 by order of her cousin, Queen Elizabeth I of England.
An executioner is a person whose job was to carry out a death sentence.
Henri III was a king of France in the 1500s. He was killed in 1589.
A friar is a man in a religious group who lives simply and travels to help people. Here, one of them attacked the king.
The front lines are the places in a war where the fighting happens, closest to the enemy.
The two Opium Wars were fought in the 1800s between Britain and China, partly over Britain selling a drug called opium there.
A pekingese is a small dog from China with long, silky fur and a flat face. Chinese emperors once kept them in palaces.
Looty is a name based on loot, which means things taken by force. The dog was taken from a palace by soldiers.
To condemn is to say that something is very bad or wrong. Here, writers called small dogs useless.
A lapdog is a small, gentle dog that is kept to sit on its owner's lap.
Frivolity means silly behavior about things that do not matter much.
Excess means more than is needed. Here, people saw tiny pampered dogs as a sign of wasting money.
Canine means to do with dogs. The word also names a dog's sharp pointed tooth.
Jane Austen was an English writer who lived from 1775 to 1817. She wrote novels such as Pride and Prejudice and Mansfield Park.
Pugmania is a made-up word for a craze for pugs, when everyone wanted one.
A poodle is a dog with thick, curly fur, often trimmed in fancy shapes.
A Labrador retriever is a large, friendly dog that is often used to fetch things and help people.
Pooch is a casual word for a dog.
A pram is a baby carriage. It is a British word. Americans say stroller.
Gen Z is the group of people born from about the late 1990s to the early 2010s.
A pollster is a person or company that asks many people questions to find out what they think.
Ipsos is a company that does polls and surveys.
To fork out is to spend money, often a lot of it and without being very happy about it.
